name: welsche haube
_about: THE WELSCHE HAUBE, the Renaissance cap of a German tower (the Frauenkirche's in Munich, 1525): a copper BULB on an eave ring set on the tower's head -- an onion struck from two radii (bulge, neck), rising without a drum, ribbed up its corners -- then a neck, a little knob, the rod, the gilt ball and the cross. Place it at the middle of the tower's head; `sides` faces to it (8 over an octagon), its faces on the axes like the tower's (`turn` -0.5: corners on them). Build without 'bulb ribs' for a smooth one. For a helm with open lanterns and a second bulb, use `baroque-helm`.

params._R: the bulb's radius at its eave (to its corners); the eave ring footH tall, its skirt flaring footOut past it at the foot
params._bulge: the bulb's two radii in half-widths (profiles.js onion): bulge 1 rises vertical from the eave, more swells out past it; neck the concave draw to the point -- small, a short sharp point (height R * sqrt(1 + 2 neck) at bulge 1)
params._knobR: the neck (knobR / 2 across, 0.7 knobR tall) and the little knob on it (an onion of knobBulge, knobNeck)
params._rodH: the rod (rodR, rodH), the ball (ballR in radius, a drop 2.1 ballR tall) and the cross (crossH, its bars crossW); haube_height() in tools/archgen/frauenkirche_munich.py adds it all up

foot._about: the eave ring the bulb stands on, its copper skirt flaring footOut past it at the foot

bulb._about: the bulb: an onion (bulge 1: rising vertical from its eave and not swelling past it, as Munich's; more: an onion) drawn in to its point (neck)

bulb ribs._about: the standing ribs up its corners

neck._about: the neck out of the bulb's point
